stories.headline: French cost-of-living protests turn into nationwide riots; ~1,500 shops looted or damaged

key_facts.fact: On Saturday, October 17, demonstrations across France against rising living costs and declining public services spiralled into some of the worst rioting the country has seen in decades.
key_facts.excerpt: Rioting erupted in cities across France on Saturday as demonstrations against rising living costs and declining public services spiralled out of control in some of the worst violence the country has witnessed for decades.

key_facts.fact: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez put turnout at around 550,000; the CGT union estimated 800,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Around 550,000 people had participated in the demonstrations across the country, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said. The CGT union told Reuters it estimated protesters at 800,000 people.

key_facts.fact: Police arrested about 1,800 people and more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured, per the BBC citing the interior ministry.
key_facts.excerpt: Police arrested about 1,800 people on Saturday... More than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured in the unrest on Saturday, France's interior ministry said.

key_facts.fact: In Limoges the city hall was set ablaze, in Marseille protesters broke into city hall, and in Lyon the tourist office was torched.
key_facts.excerpt: In Limoges, the city hall was set ablaze; in Marseille, black-clad protesters broke into city hall and defaced the building with anarchic graffiti, and in Lyon, protesters torched the city's tourist office.

key_facts.fact: About 1,500 businesses were hit; Carrefour CEO Alexandre Bompard said 50 Carrefour stores were targeted with repairs over €10 million, and warned the total bill could reach several hundred million euros.
key_facts.excerpt: Bompard... estimated that the unrest had affected around 1,500 businesses nationwide. He warned that the total damage bill could run into several hundred million euros

key_facts.fact: Sephora closed its entire French store network from 5pm Saturday through Sunday; Louis Vuitton, Dior, Celine, Burberry, Lacoste and Apple stores were among those looted or damaged.
key_facts.excerpt: Sephora closed its entire French store network from 5pm on Saturday and kept stores shut on Sunday after several branches were ransacked

key_facts.fact: France 24 notes purchasing power has dwindled since 2024 and fuel prices have soared since the start of the US-Iran war earlier this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Purchasing power in France has dwindled since 2024, while the price of fuel has soared since the start of the US-Iran war earlier this year.

key_facts.fact: President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence in a televised address on Sunday, promising those responsible for looting would be held accountable.
key_facts.excerpt: President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence in a televised address on Sunday, promising that those responsible for looting would be held accountable.

stories.headline: Iran says two supertankers hit mines in Hormuz as Brent closes at 5-month high near $110

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC said two oil tankers, each carrying about two million barrels of crude, caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz while using a route not authorised by Tehran; the claims were not independently verified.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has said two oil tankers, each carrying about two million barrels of crude oil, caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

key_facts.fact: UKMTO said at least 10 vessels were attacked in or near the strait in the week since last Sunday, a weekly high since the war began in February, with 23 attacks so far in October.
key_facts.excerpt: at least 10 vessels have been attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz since last Sunday, a weekly high since war broke out in February, and 23 attacks were recorded since the start of the month

key_facts.fact: Kpler data show oil flows through the strait fell from nearly 20.8 million barrels on October 8 to 2.9 million on October 11.
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly 20.8 million barrels of oil passed through on October 8, but only 2.9 million on October 11, according to Kpler data.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude settled at $109.86 on Friday, October 16, its highest close since May 19, while WTI rose 3.5% to $101.41, its first close above $100 since September.
key_facts.excerpt: It ended the week at $109.86 per barrel, still its highest closing level since May 19. U.S. crude oil... jumped 3.5% Friday to close at $101.41 per barrel.

key_facts.fact: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday the strait would reopen on the sixth day if the US meets Iran's seven-day proposal conditions (ending the naval blockade, lifting oil sanctions, ceasefire on all fronts), with talks on the seventh day.
key_facts.excerpt: "If they comply with our conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will reopen on the sixth day, and negotiations will begin on the seventh day," Araghchi said

key_facts.fact: CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said on October 16 the US naval blockade has prevented at least $25 billion in Iranian crude exports and Washington has frozen nearly $350 million in Iranian crypto assets.
key_facts.excerpt: The US naval blockade of Iran has prevented at least $25 billion in crude oil exports, and Washington has frozen nearly $350 million in Iranian cryptocurrency assets, the commander of US Central Command (CENTCOM) said.

key_facts.fact: Iran's parliament on October 18 approved UN-sanctioned former missile-industry chief Mehrdad Akhlaqi Ketabchi as defense minister, 237 votes to 15.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's parliament on October 18 approved Mehrdad Akhlaqi Ketabchi as the country's new defense minister... He received 237 votes in favor and 15 against

stories.headline: Trump suspends new Russia sanctions law for 60 days, drawing bipartisan backlash and Zelensky's rebuke

key_facts.fact: Trump signed an executive order on Friday, October 16, putting on hold a sweeping Russia sanctions package that he had signed into law, citing the national interest.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump on Friday signed an executive order that puts on hold a sweeping new sanctions package targeting

key_facts.fact: The blocked sanctions were due to take effect two days later; Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the suspension is a 60-day pause to analyse the impact on the US and global economy.
key_facts.excerpt: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that the suspension would consist of a 60-day pause to allow for the Trump administration to analyse the impact

key_facts.fact: The law gave Trump power to levy tariffs of up to 100% on imports from the top five buyers of Russian oil and gas, notably China and India, and sanctioned Putin, Russian banks and the shadow fleet.
key_facts.excerpt: The new US sanctions law took aim at Russia's economy by giving Trump broad powers to levy tariffs of up to 100% on imports from the top five purchasers of Russian oil and gas – most significantly China and India.

key_facts.fact: Republican senators Ted Cruz, John Cornyn and Thom Tillis criticised the move alongside Democrats; Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it 'an important and truly historic moment'.
key_facts.excerpt: Texas Senator Ted Cruz, a Trump ally, called waiving the sanctions a mistake... John Cornyn called the move "reckless".

key_facts.fact: Zelensky said the decision 'definitely helps only the Russians' and pointed to Russian overnight attacks on 15 Ukrainian energy facilities.
key_facts.excerpt: "The decision to undo all of this, to block all of it, seems wrong to me," Zelenskyy said in a post on X. "And it definitely helps only the Russians."

key_facts.fact: The move follows a Trump-Putin deal easing sanctions so Russia can supply 4.8 million metric tons of diesel to global markets, which experts say will barely move prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump's agreement with Putin was for Russia to supply the global market with 4.8 million metric tons of diesel, the equivalent of about ten days of U.S. domestic demand

stories.headline: China's Q3 GDP growth picks up to 4.5% as AI-driven exports offset weak domestic demand

key_facts.fact: China's GDP grew 4.5% year on year in Q3 2026, up from 4.3% in Q2, with 4.6% growth over the first three quarters, the National Bureau of Statistics said Monday, October 19.
key_facts.excerpt: China's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 4.5 percent year on year in the third quarter (Q3) of 2026... The growth rate was higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent... 4.6 percent year on year in the first three quarters.

key_facts.fact: Q2's 4.3% was the slowest growth since 2022; Q3 beat the 4.41% Wind consensus forecast.
key_facts.excerpt: The third-quarter growth was above the 4.41 per cent consensus forecast of economists surveyed by Chinese financial data provider Wind.

key_facts.fact: The figure sits at the bottom of Beijing's 4.5%-5% annual target, and the BBC says the AI boom helped boost exports.
key_facts.excerpt: The latest figure is at the bottom end of Beijing's annual growth target of 4.5%-5%

key_facts.fact: High-tech manufacturing rose 14.3%, and output of industrial robots and lithium-ion batteries rose 29.1% and 39.5%.
key_facts.excerpt: high-tech manufacturing up 14.3 percent. Output of industrial robots, lithium-ion batteries and 3D printing equipment jumped 29.1 percent, 39.5 percent and 62.5 percent

key_facts.fact: Property investment fell more than 20% in the first nine months, and China's trade surplus is on track to top last year's record $1.2 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: property investment fell by more than 20% in the first nine months from the same period last year

stories.headline: Nasdaq posts worst week since June as AI-debt fears, $110 oil and 5% yields hit markets

key_facts.fact: On Friday, October 16, the Nasdaq fell 2.1% and ended the week down 4.5%, its worst week since June; the S&P 500 lost 1.1% on the day and about 2% for the week.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nasdaq and S&P 500 finished Friday down a respective 2.1% and 1.2%... The Nasdaq had a four-week winning streak snapped, tumbling 4.5% over the week's five sessions.

key_facts.fact: Tech stocks shed more than $1 trillion in value Friday, and the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell for an eighth straight day, the longest streak since 2008.
key_facts.excerpt: The Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped 3.8% for its eight straight day of losses, the longest such streak since 2008.

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave fell about 12% Friday and roughly 25% for the week, with its bonds selling off to yields above 15% amid worries that debt-laden AI infrastructure firms can't repay as borrowing costs rise.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia-backed CoreWeave slumped 12%, bringing its loss over the past five sessions to about 25%. The data center operator's bonds also sold off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%.

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield traded above 5.09% after spiking to 5.33% on Wednesday's CPI; traders priced an 89% chance of a Fed hike in December after Chair Kevin Warsh spoke at an IMF event in Bangkok.
key_facts.excerpt: The 10-year Treasury yield was above 5.09%... They see an 89% likelihood of a rate hike at its December meeting

key_facts.fact: The VIX rose above 22 for the first time in four months; Bank of America's Michael Hartnett turned 'risk-off' for the next month citing yields, oil and midterm risk.
key_facts.excerpt: The sell-off sent the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) above 22 for the first time in four months.

key_facts.fact: Barclays now expects 25-basis-point Fed hikes in both December and January, after hotter-than-expected CPI and PPI readings.
key_facts.excerpt: Barclays now expects 25-basis-point hikes each in December and January.

stories.headline: Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica and Vodafone sign LoI for joint satellite spectrum bid vs Starlink

key_facts.fact: On October 19, Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica and Vodafone signed a letter of intent to explore a joint bid for future Mobile Satellite Services (MSS) spectrum in Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica and Vodafone have signed a Letter of Intent to explore a potential joint bid for the future allocation of spectrum for Mobile Satellite Services (MSS) in Europe.

key_facts.fact: The operators will build ground infrastructure and coordination functions in Europe but will not invest directly in a satellite constellation, which will come from a satellite partner still to be selected.
key_facts.excerpt: the four operators plan to establish key ground network infrastructure as well as critical coordination and monitoring functions in Europe, without investing directly in a satellite constellation. This will be provided by a satellite partner still to be selected.

key_facts.fact: The group says it will give all mobile operators open, non-discriminatory access to offer direct-to-device (D2D) services, in support of the European Commission's sovereignty goals.
key_facts.excerpt: it will provide all Mobile Network Operators with open and non-discriminatory access to offer Direct-to-Device (D2D) services to their customers.

key_facts.fact: The bid targets the share of 2 GHz airwaves the EU has proposed reserving for a European operator, and aims to fend off Elon Musk's Starlink.
key_facts.excerpt: exploring a joint bid for a share of airwaves that the European Union has proposed reserving for a local operator... as they try to stave off competition from Elon Musk's Starlink service.

key_facts.fact: The LoI doesn't replace existing partnerships; Deutsche Telekom already works with SpaceX's Starlink Mobile and Iridium on satellite D2D and IoT.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies said the agreement would not replace their existing satellite partnerships. Deutsche Telekom has been working with SpaceX's Starlink Mobile and with Iridium on satellite D2D and IoT

stories.headline: FDA approves Roche's Enspryng as first at-home injectable treatment for thyroid eye disease

key_facts.fact: Roche announced on October 16 that the FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab) for adults with thyroid eye disease (TED), the first at-home subcutaneous treatment option.
key_facts.excerpt: Roche... announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Enspryng® (satralizumab) for the treatment of adults with thyroid eye disease (TED), providing patients with the first and only at-home subcutaneous treatment option.

key_facts.fact: Enspryng is a first-in-class anti-IL-6 receptor antibody, dosed every four weeks during maintenance, and can be self-administered or given by a caregiver.
key_facts.excerpt: offering the first at-home SC treatment option every four weeks during maintenance phase

key_facts.fact: In Phase III SatraGO-2, 52.9% of patients on Enspryng achieved a proptosis (eye-bulging) response vs 23.4% on placebo, and 60.7% vs 25.8% saw reduced double vision; SatraGO-1 missed its primary endpoint.
key_facts.excerpt: SatraGO-2 achieved significant and clinically meaningful difference in proptosis response (52.9% in the Enspryng group compared to 23.4% in the placebo group) and in diplopia reduction (60.7%... compared to 25.8%...)

key_facts.fact: TED is a rare autoimmune disease affecting about 155 per 100,000 people in the US; this is Enspryng's second indication after neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder in 2020.
key_facts.excerpt: TED is a rare autoimmune disease affecting approximately 155 out of every 100,000 people in the US

sources.title: FDA approves Roche's Enspryng, a first-in-class IL-6R inhibitor, as the first and only at-home subcutaneous treatment option for thyroid eye disease (TED)
